title: AraLearn authoring GPT system prompt
decision_contribution: Defines distinct planning/build/audit/repair/reaudit/publish rounds, microsequence write unit, revisions, comments and explicit publication.
limitation: Implementation-specific and not automatically normative for ARA.

title: AraLearn didactic model
decision_contribution: Provides microsequence rationale, dependency continuity, worked examples, human curation and mobile/offline context.
limitation: Pedagogical rationale is not a universal domain model.

title: AraLearn non-punitive study state
decision_contribution: Distinguishes functional state, situated observations and prohibited behavioural inferences.
limitation: Does not specify collaborative authorship lifecycle.

title: P1 synthesis
decision_contribution: Handoff for response, attempts, feedback, consequences, accessibility precedence and output authority.
limitation: Covers study/practice rather than authoring lifecycle.

title: P2 synthesis
decision_contribution: Handoff for sequence, examples, scaffolding, snapshots and contextual placement.
limitation: Does not decide reusable-unit architecture.

title: P3 synthesis
decision_contribution: Defines bounded AI assistance, human approval, provenance, contestability and dual channels.
limitation: Does not define institutional authoring workflow.

title: P4 synthesis
decision_contribution: Defines protocol/condition snapshots, provenance, governance, rights and role-oriented analytics.
limitation: Does not define production review/publication policy.

title: Guidance for generative AI in education and research
decision_contribution: Supports human-centred validation, privacy protection, policy and pedagogical design for GenAI.
limitation: Global guidance; not a product workflow specification.

title: Recommendation on Open Educational Resources
decision_contribution: Supports reuse, adaptation, redistribution, quality assurance, accessibility, policy and sustainability.
limitation: Applies to openly licensed resources, not confidential or private content by default.

title: PROV-O: The PROV Ontology
decision_contribution: Provides Entity/Activity/Agent, derivation, revision, specialization and bundles for interoperable provenance.
limitation: Too broad to adopt wholesale as the internal domain model.

title: Web Annotation Data Model
decision_contribution: Provides structured bodies, targets, selectors, motivations, canonical identity and provenance for situated annotations.
limitation: Web IRIs/JSON-LD may not fit the first implementation directly.

title: C2PA Technical Specification 2.4
decision_contribution: Provides tamper-evident content provenance and attestations; useful as external provenance comparison.
limitation: Optimized for media authenticity, not educational workflow semantics.

title: C2PA Guiding Principles
decision_contribution: Separates verifiable provenance assertions from value judgments and emphasizes user/organizational needs.
limitation: Does not establish educational quality or authorship rights.

title: Contributor Role Taxonomy (CRediT)
decision_contribution: Demonstrates transparent, structured contribution roles beyond a single author label.
limitation: Research-output roles need adaptation for educational production.

title: Creative Commons licenses
decision_contribution: Defines reuse, adaptation, attribution, ShareAlike, NonCommercial and NoDerivatives constraints.
limitation: License selection/compatibility can require legal interpretation.

title: Considerations for licensors and licensees
decision_contribution: Requires attention to scope, version, attribution, adaptations, third-party rights and non-revocability.
limitation: Guidance is not jurisdiction-specific legal advice.

title: Higher Education Course Design Rubric
decision_contribution: Shows alignment across objectives, assessments, materials, activities, technology, support and accessibility, with essential standards.
limitation: Full rubric annotations are membership-controlled; design quality does not prove learning outcomes.

title: Quality Matters course review process
decision_contribution: Distinguishes self, internal and official reviews and uses multi-reviewer teams including SME/external reviewer roles.
limitation: Certification process is institutional and not a universal ARA workflow.

title: OSCQR course review rubric and process
decision_contribution: Provides formative, non-evaluative review, action plans, refresh cycles, accessibility and multiple reviewer models.
limitation: Rubric targets online course design and does not cover every ARA artifact type.

title: Approving a pull request with required reviews
decision_contribution: Demonstrates comment/approve/request-changes states, changed-file review and approval invalidation after changes.
limitation: Software review mechanics are analogies, not educational requirements.

title: About code owners
decision_contribution: Demonstrates scoped ownership, automatic reviewer requests and protected approval policies.
limitation: File ownership differs from pedagogical or institutional authority.

title: Open edX Content Libraries overview
decision_contribution: Shows centralized reusable content, cross-course use, publishing and library-specific roles.
limitation: Sync/update semantics may not meet ARA's immutable snapshot and offline requirements.

title: Open edX course roles and permissions
decision_contribution: Separates editor, staff/publisher and auditor/read-only roles.
limitation: Role set is platform-specific and not sufficient for research governance.

title: Open edX library publishing statuses
decision_contribution: Provides draft, published and published-with-pending-edits states; only published content is reusable.
limitation: Does not define AI provenance or ARA's repair/re-audit lifecycle.

title: H5P reuse content
decision_contribution: Shows import/export and copy/paste reuse of subcontent within supported containers.
limitation: Copy-based reuse has limited cross-site lineage and update propagation.

title: H5P best practices and library versions
decision_contribution: Shows reusable libraries, dependencies, multiple versions and controlled updates.
limitation: Library versioning concerns code/content types more than pedagogical units.

title: H5P licensing
decision_contribution: Demonstrates explicit content/code licensing and reuse expectations.
limitation: Does not by itself solve per-asset license compatibility.

title: Human-AI Co-Creation of Worked Examples for Programming Classes
decision_contribution: Shows AI-generated starting drafts edited by instructors and evaluates explanation quality.
limitation: Single domain and resource type; does not establish autonomous publication.

title: PedaCo-Gen: Scaffolding Pedagogical Agency in Human-AI Collaborative Video Authoring
decision_contribution: Supports intermediate representations, educator review/refinement and pedagogical-agency scaffolding.
limitation: Small expert study focused on instructional video generation.

title: Can We Trust AI-Generated Educational Content?
decision_contribution: Blind evaluation found some AI resources comparable to peer-created resources while noting exemplar mirroring and limited scope.
limitation: Perceived quality in introductory programming; not long-term learning or broad domains.

title: Evaluating LLM Workflows for Generating Clinical Communication Assessment Items
decision_contribution: Constrained workflows outperformed exploratory branching; most items still required SME revision.
limitation: High-stakes clinical domain; workflow and rubric specific.

title: ELI-Why: Evaluating the Pedagogical Utility of Language Model Explanations
decision_contribution: Shows frequent mismatch between generated explanations and intended learner level/information need.
limitation: Explanations benchmark; not course-scale authorship.

title: COGENT: Curriculum-oriented Grade-appropriate Educational Content
decision_contribution: Shows benefits of explicit curriculum components, readability controls and multidimensional evaluation.
limitation: Focused on passages and science curricula; evaluation includes model judges.

title: LLMs are Biased Teachers
decision_contribution: Finds demographic bias in generated/selected educational content, supporting bias review and bounded personalization.
limitation: Synthetic/evaluative setup; does not prescribe full mitigation workflow.

title: IDEAlign: Comparing Ideas of LLMs to Domain Experts
decision_contribution: Finds automated similarity metrics and LLM judges fall short of expert nuance; useful for triage rather than substitution.
limitation: Educational datasets are limited; not a publication workflow study.

title: PeerCheck: Enhancing LLM-Generated Academic Reviews
decision_contribution: Shows LLM-human review differences and variable effects of prompting/RAG; review assistance remains model-dependent.
limitation: Academic paper review differs from course QA.

title: ReviewEval: Evaluation Framework for AI-Generated Reviews
decision_contribution: Operationalizes accuracy, depth, constructiveness and guideline adherence with iterative refinement.
limitation: Evaluation metrics remain domain- and benchmark-dependent.

title: Is LLM a Reliable Reviewer?
decision_contribution: Finds LLM review assistance useful but error-prone, weak on long inputs and critical feedback.
limitation: Academic paper review; models studied may age quickly.

title: Learning to Judge: LLMs Designing and Applying Evaluation Rubrics
decision_contribution: LLMs can generate interpretable criteria but scoring reliability degrades for factual and knowledge-intensive tasks.
limitation: Does not justify self-authored rubrics as sole authority.

title: Evaluating a blended course: why Quality Matters
decision_contribution: Illustrates iterative self-evaluation and rubric-guided course improvement.
limitation: Single course/context; does not establish causal effectiveness of the rubric.

title: OpenCourseWare Observatory
decision_contribution: Shows reuse, freshness and fitness-for-use problems across OCW repositories.
limitation: Older ecosystem sample; metrics do not map directly to ARA.

title: Scaling Success: Peer Grading Strategies
decision_contribution: Highlights no universally optimal reviewer-weighting strategy and supports hybrid/formative review designs.
limitation: Peer grading of student work differs from authoring QA.

title: Software Citation Implementation Challenges
decision_contribution: Supports unique identification, persistence, accessibility, specificity, attribution and version-aware citation.
limitation: Software citation principles require adaptation for educational units.
